description: Hand-authored executable package-resolution scenarios; not third-party npm certification.

cases.description: Resolve relative CommonJS imports across a three-file dependency chain.
Repeated extensionless/explicit loads share the same export object.

files.main.cjs: const a = require('./counter'); a.value++; const b = require('./counter.js'); console.log(a === b, b.value);

cases.description: A cycle observes already-published exports without reevaluating the module.

files.a.js: exports.ready = 'a-start'; const b = require('./b'); exports.seen = b.seen; exports.ready = 'a-done';

cases.description: JSON modules are parsed once and cached by resolved filename.

files.main.cjs: const a = require('./config.json'); a.value++; const b = require('./config.json'); console.log(a === b, b.value);

cases.description: A relative package directory resolves its package.json main.
A bare specifier resolves a captured node_modules package, not a registry install.
A package uses its nearest nested dependency rather than the project-level version.
Scoped package exports resolve an explicit public subpath.

files.node_modules/@fixture/math/lib/add.cjs: module.exports = function(a, b) { return a + b; };

cases.description: CommonJS selects the require branch rather than import/default.
ESM selects the import branch rather than require/default.
ESM links named exports across relative module boundaries.

files.main.mjs: import { base } from './lib/base.mjs'; import { add } from './lib/add.mjs'; console.log(add(base, 2));
files.lib/add.mjs: export function add(a, b) { return a + b; }

cases.description: An imported binding remains live after a function mutates its exporting module.

files.main.mjs: import { value, increment } from './counter.mjs'; console.log(value); increment(); console.log(value);
files.counter.mjs: export let value = 1; export function increment() { value++; }

cases.description: A re-export forwards a named binding through a barrel module.
The nearest package type determines the goal for .js entrypoints and dependencies.
A named package resolves its own exported entry without node_modules.
A package-local hash import resolves through the imports map.
An existing private file is not importable when the exports map excludes it.

files.main.cjs: try { require('fixture-private/private.js'); console.log('unexpected access'); } catch (error) { console.log(error.code); }

cases.description: A user module loads node:path and exposes its result to the entrypoint.

files.join.js: const path = require('node:path'); module.exports = function(a, b) { return path.posix.join(a, b); };

cases.description: A dependency reads an input file and writes an independently checked output file.

files.writer.cjs: const fs = require('node:fs'); module.exports = function() { const data = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('input.json', 'utf8')); fs.writeFileSync('result.json', JSON.stringify({answer: data.value * 2}) + '\n'); };

cases.description: A captured package's native Blob produces independent promised byte arrays without exposing its source buffer.

files.main.cjs: const blob = require('fixture-blob')(); const pending = blob.bytes(); console.log(pending instanceof Promise); (async function () { const first = await pending; const second = await blob.bytes(); const raw = await blob.arrayBuffer(); console.log(first instanceof Uint8Array, first.byteOffset, first.length, first.join(',')); console.log(first !== second, first.buffer !== second.buffer, first.buffer !== raw); first.fill(8); console.log(second.join(','), new Uint8Array(raw).join(','), blob.size, blob.type); })();
files.node_modules/fixture-blob/index.cjs: const { Blob } = require('node:buffer'); module.exports = function () { const source = new Uint8Array([99,0,255,65,88]); const blob = new Blob([source.subarray(1,4)], {type:'APPLICATION/OCTET-STREAM'}); source.fill(7); return blob; };

cases.description: An ESM dependency preserves viewed binary bytes, BOMs and invalid UTF-8 through native Blob byte reads and slices.

files.main.mjs: import { inner, payload } from './payload.mjs'; (async function () { console.log((await payload.bytes()).join(',')); console.log((await payload.slice(3,-2).bytes()).join(',')); console.log(JSON.stringify(await inner.text())); console.log((await new Blob().bytes()).length); })();
files.payload.mjs: import { Blob } from 'node:buffer'; const input = new Uint8Array([9,239,187,191,255,0,65,8]); export const inner = new Blob([new DataView(input.buffer,1,6)]); export const payload = new Blob([inner,'é','\ud800']); input.fill(0);

cases.description: Each generator-produced mutable buffer is snapshotted before its next mutation across a CommonJS boundary.

files.main.cjs: const make = require('./parts.cjs'); const blob = make(); blob.bytes().then(bytes => console.log(bytes.join(','), blob.size));
files.parts.cjs: module.exports = function () { const source = new Uint8Array([65]); function* parts() { yield source; source[0]=66; yield source; source[0]=67; yield new Blob(['D']); } return new Blob(parts()); };

cases.description: Compare byte-read and array-buffer completion ordering without treating native promise creation as synchronous fulfillment.

files.main.cjs: const blob = require('./payload.cjs'); const order=['start']; const first=blob.bytes().then(bytes=>{order.push('bytes');return bytes;}); const second=blob.arrayBuffer().then(bytes=>{order.push('buffer');return bytes;}); order.push('sync'); Promise.all([first,second]).then(([bytes,buffer])=>{console.log(order.join(','));bytes[0]=0;console.log(new Uint8Array(buffer).join(','),blob.size);});

cases.description: A module reads input bytes, snapshots a Blob, awaits its native byte array and writes an independently checked file.

files.writer.cjs: const fs = require('node:fs'); const { Blob } = require('node:buffer'); module.exports = async function () { const input = fs.readFileSync('input.txt'); const blob = new Blob([input]); input.fill(0); const bytes = await blob.bytes(); fs.writeFileSync('result.txt', bytes); bytes.fill(0); return blob.size; };
